title: Return to Nephi
summary: Limhi and his people return to the city of Nephi and dwell there in peace.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi and his people returned to the city of Nephi and began to dwell in the land again in peace.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people are settled in the city.
unspecified_visual_details: Architecture, clothing, and time of day.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the place from which they returned.

title: Oppression Begins
summary: After many days, the Lamanites enter the borders and oppress the Nephites, burdening and driving them while refraining from killing them because of their king’s oath.

explicit_facts.text: After many days, the Lamanites became angry and came into the borders of the land.
They refrained from killing the Nephites because of their king’s oath to Limhi, but struck them, burdened them, and drove them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamanites drive burdened Nephites.
unspecified_visual_details: Garments, weapons, exact burdens, and the Lamanite king's identity.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 4 says this fulfilled the word of the Lord; it does not describe a visible divine event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show killing in this scene.

title: Surrounded
summary: Lamanites surround the Nephites on every side, leaving them unable to deliver themselves.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites surrounded the Nephites on every side, and the Nephites had no way to deliver themselves.
The events fulfilled the word of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A wide view can convey encirclement without showing a battle.
unspecified_visual_details: Terrain, structures, and number of Lamanites.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not depict the Lord; the verse describes no appearance.

title: The People Demand Battle
summary: The people murmur against Limhi and desire battle; their complaints afflict him, and he grants their request.

explicit_facts.text: The people murmured against the king and desired battle; their complaints sorely afflicted him, and he granted their request.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people are gathered before Limhi.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact words, gestures, and the setting within the city.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent spoken words.

title: First Battle
summary: Limhi’s people arm themselves and go against the Lamanites, who defeat them, drive them back, and slay many.

explicit_facts.text: The people gathered, armed themselves, and went against the Lamanites.
The Lamanites beat them, drove them back, and slew many.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fighting may be shown without graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: Tactics, weapons, armor, and identities of the slain.
prohibited_inventions: No gore, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Mourning
summary: The people mourn their dead, and many widows cry from day to day in fear of the Lamanites.
characters: children and relatives of the slain

explicit_facts.text: Widows mourned their husbands, children their father, and brothers their brethren.
Many widows cried mightily from day to day because of fear of the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mourners may be shown grieving together.
unspecified_visual_details: Identities and appearance of individual mourners; whether the dead are present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a burial or show the earlier deaths occurring now.

title: Second Battle
summary: The widows’ cries stir the remainder of Limhi’s people to anger; they go to battle again and are driven back with much loss.

explicit_facts.text: The widows’ cries stirred the remainder of Limhi’s people to anger; they went to battle again, were driven back, and suffered much loss.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The battle may be shown as the people retreat.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact location, tactics, and number of casualties.
prohibited_inventions: Do not merge this battle with the first or third.

title: Third Battle and Return
summary: The people go to battle a third time and suffer similarly; those not slain return to the city of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: The people went a third time and suffered in the same manner; those not slain returned to the city of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Survivors may be shown returning toward the city.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and battlefield appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add an outcome beyond their suffering similarly.

title: Humbling and Prayer
summary: The people humble themselves under bondage, submit to burdens and abuse, and cry to God all day for deliverance.

explicit_facts.text: They humbled themselves to the dust, submitted to bondage, and endured being smitten, driven, and burdened.
They cried mightily to God all day, asking for deliverance from their afflictions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown praying while under oppression.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact location and individual participants.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text describes prayer but no visible appearance of God.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a miraculous rescue.

title: Burdens Eased
summary: The Lord hears their cries and begins softening the Lamanites’ hearts; their burdens are eased, but they remain in bondage.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord heard their cries and began softening the Lamanites’ hearts; their burdens were eased, but they were not delivered from bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamanites may be shown easing the people's burdens.
unspecified_visual_details: How the change in the Lamanites’ hearts appears physically.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: No divine appearance or release from bondage is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a visible supernatural intervention or their release.

title: Prosperity by Degrees
summary: The people gradually prosper, raising more grain and keeping flocks and herds so they do not suffer hunger.

explicit_facts.text: They gradually prospered, raised more grain, and kept flocks and herds so they did not suffer hunger.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Grain and livestock can show improved provision.
unspecified_visual_details: Crop and livestock varieties, farm layout, and scale.
prohibited_inventions: Do not imply freedom from bondage.

title: Support for Widows
summary: Because there are more women than men, Limhi commands each man to support widows and their children so they will not perish from hunger; the people comply.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi commanded every man to support widows and their children so they would not perish from hunger; they did so because many had been slain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Men may be shown sharing provisions with widows and children.
unspecified_visual_details: Provisions and manner of distribution.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent Limhi’s spoken words.

title: Guarded City
summary: The people stay together as much as possible and secure their grain and flocks. Limhi goes outside the city walls only with guards, fearing capture.

explicit_facts.text: The people kept together as much as possible and secured their grain and flocks.
Limhi did not go outside the city walls without guards, fearing he might fall into Lamanite hands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi may be shown beyond the walls accompanied by guards.
unspecified_visual_details: The walls’ appearance and storage arrangements.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an actual capture.

title: Watch for Noah’s Priests
summary: Limhi has his people watch the land for the priests who fled into the wilderness, intending to punish them for entering by night and carrying off grain and precious things.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi caused the people to watch the land to capture the priests who fled into the wilderness and had stolen the daughters of the Lamanites.
The priests entered the land of Nephi by night, carried off grain and precious things, and the people laid wait for them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown keeping watch.
unspecified_visual_details: Watchers’ positions and whether any priests are seen.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The priests’ thefts are reported past events, not happening in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the priests committing the past theft.

title: Ammon Arrives
summary: After a period without disturbance, Limhi discovers Ammon and his brethren outside the city gates and, mistaking them for Noah’s priests, has them bound and imprisoned.

explicit_facts.text: There was no more disturbance between the Lamanites and Limhi’s people until Ammon and his brethren came.
Outside the gates with his guard, Limhi discovered Ammon and his brethren, supposed them to be Noah’s priests, and had them bound and cast into prison.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon and his brethren may be shown being bound under guard.
unspecified_visual_details: Number and identities of Ammon’s brethren and prison design.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prisoners being killed.

title: Recognition and Joy
summary: Limhi learns the men are his brethren from Zarahemla, not Noah’s priests, and is filled with great joy.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi found they were his brethren from Zarahemla, not Noah’s priests, and was filled with exceedingly great joy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi and the men may be shown together after recognition.
unspecified_visual_details: How they were released and gestures of recognition.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent an embrace or dialogue.

title: Searchers in the Wilderness
summary: Before Ammon arrived, Limhi’s search party failed to find Zarahemla, became lost in the wilderness, found a land covered with dry bones, mistook it for Zarahemla, and returned to Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi sent a small party to find Zarahemla; they could not find it and were lost in the wilderness.
They found a peopled land covered with dry bones, supposed it was Zarahemla, and returned to Nephi shortly before Ammon came.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The party may be shown among the bones, without identifying the land as Zarahemla.
unspecified_visual_details: Route, exact number of searchers, and extent of the land.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The search is reported retrospectively and predates Ammon’s arrival.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the bone-covered land as Zarahemla; the searchers only supposed it was.

title: The Record on Plates
summary: The searchers bring a record engraved on plates of ore concerning the people whose bones they found.

explicit_facts.text: They brought a record of the people whose bones they found, engraved on plates of ore.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The plates may be shown in the searchers’ possession.
unspecified_visual_details: Plate size, appearance, and engraving style.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict interpretation of the plates.

title: News of Mosiah’s Gift
summary: Ammon tells Limhi that Mosiah has a gift from God to interpret the engravings; Limhi and Ammon rejoice.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon told Limhi that Mosiah had a gift from God to interpret the engravings; both rejoiced.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi and Ammon may be shown together as the news is shared.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact words, gestures, and whether the plates are present.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mosiah is not described as present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Mosiah or a visible divine gift.

title: Sorrow for Losses
summary: Ammon and his brethren mourn the slain, the people’s sins, Abinadi’s death, and Alma’s departure with his people; they would gladly have joined them and had themselves covenanted to serve God.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and his brethren sorrowed because many of their brethren had been slain.
They mourned the sins caused by Noah and his priests, Abinadi’s death, and Alma and his people’s departure.
They did not know where Alma’s group had fled and would gladly have joined them; they had covenanted to serve God and keep his commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon and his brethren may be shown grieving together.
unspecified_visual_details: Manner of mourning and the location of Alma’s group.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Abinadi and Alma’s group are mentioned, not shown present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier death or departure as happening now.

title: Limhi’s Covenant
summary: After Ammon’s arrival, Limhi and many of his people enter a covenant with God to serve him and keep his commandments.

explicit_facts.text: Since Ammon came, Limhi and many of his people entered a covenant with God to serve him and keep his commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi and some of the people may be shown gathered.
unspecified_visual_details: Ritual, spoken words, and exact participants.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict baptism here.

title: Baptism Deferred
summary: Limhi and many desire baptism, but no one in the land has authority from God; Ammon declines, and they wait rather than forming a church or being baptized then.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi and many desired baptism, but no one in the land had authority from God; Ammon declined, considering himself unworthy.
They did not then form a church, waiting upon the Spirit, and desired to become like Alma and his brethren.
They desired baptism as a testimony of willingness to serve God wholeheartedly, but delayed it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown gathered and waiting, with no baptism taking place.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact words, setting, and outward signs of waiting.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Baptism is desired but not performed at this time.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict baptism, church formation, or invented speech.

title: Seeking Deliverance
summary: Ammon and his people, together with Limhi and his people, focus on delivering themselves from the Lamanites and bondage.

explicit_facts.text: The study of Ammon and his people and Limhi and his people was to deliver themselves from the Lamanites and bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The groups may be shown conferring about deliverance.
unspecified_visual_details: Their plans, methods, and any action toward escape.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a plan or depict an escape.
